info.name: Smart-LIMS API
info.description:
Smart-LIMS API requests. Select Smart-LIMS Local and enter inputs and credentials as local values. Protected requests support bearer and cookie authentication. State changes and mail require separate local opt-ins as applicable.

### Disposable test workflow

Use the local desktop agent or the project's `postman/run-smart-lims-api.cjs` fixture runner with a freshly exported copy of this collection. Run the Backend against `smart_lims_test_db` on a loopback HTTP origin, with Mailpit and a disposable administrator configured as a laboratory reviewer. Provide `baseUrl`, `verifiedTestDatabase`, `allowTestWrites`, and `allowEmailSending` in the local run context. Write and mail opt-ins default to false. Keep credentials and sessions local.

The fixture runner sequences account setup, patient and catalog data, orders and appointments, then visit arrival, specimen receipt and attestation, draft and reviewer approval, publication, patient results and archive reads. Cancellation, rejection and no-show use separate fixtures. For manual runs, keep the cookie jar through CSRF, cookie login and logout, use the intended role for each request, and carry forward IDs and versions after each transition.

### Native Collection Runner (local)

An opt-in native dependency sequence is available. In the local environment set `smartLimsNativeRun=true` and `smartLimsNativeFixtures` to a JSON object keyed by exact request name. Per-request values may reference local environment inputs using `{{variableName}}`. Start the full collection with Login at the top of the Runner request list. Keep credentials as local environment values, leave Keep variable values disabled, and leave response persistence off. Prepare disposable fixtures, Mailpit confirmation and recovery inputs, and the separate appointment/sample branches before starting. This sequence controls request order and role selection. It does not generate the auxiliary fixtures that the local Newman runner provisions. Keep the loopback, test database, write and email safeguards enabled as appropriate.

Native fixtures: use a same-day booked appointment for scheduled arrival and a separate pending order for the appended payment/refund steps. Supply local fixture overrides for order IDs and refund inputs. Use the same UUID and payload when replaying a write. Run paid cancellation and replay scenarios with the existing requests by supplying the appropriate local fixture inputs.
